project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas Fraxinus + Forestiera visual module
project_scope.note: Canonical Fraxinus species are clickable; Forestiera remains a family-reference anchor.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at the node: local Oleaceae is woody, usually opposite/subopposite, and lacks stipules. Then read leaf architecture and fruit.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Fraxinus has odd-pinnate compound leaves; Forestiera has simple leaves.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Often small; corolla may be absent in local focal genera.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Fraxinus makes a samara; Forestiera makes a one-seeded drupe.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite leaves alone are not enough—fruit type is the fast local separator.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Oleaceae is easiest locally when you pair opposite branching with the fruit: ash keys versus Forestiera drupes.

steps.title: 1 · Start with opposite ash architecture
steps.photo_role: Texas ash compound leaves + samara cluster
steps.image_credit: CC BY 2.0 · source filed as F. texensis synonym
steps.look_for: Opposite branching with odd-pinnate compound leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: This gets you to Fraxinus quickly.

steps.title: 2 · Read the samara wing
steps.look_for: Single-winged fruits; in green ash the wing runs distinctly down the seed body.
steps.why_it_matters: Samara shape separates local ash species and distinguishes ash from boxelder.

steps.title: 3 · Compare leaf-only ash
steps.look_for: Opposite odd-pinnate leaves before fruit appears.
steps.why_it_matters: Builds the vegetative doorway to the family.

steps.title: 4 · See the simple-leaved family exception
steps.image_credit: CC BY 2.0 · Petrified Forest National Park
steps.look_for: Opposite/subopposite simple leaves on a woody shrub.

comparisons.title: Oleaceae vs Rubiaceae
comparisons.rule: Rubiaceae usually has interpetiolar stipules and an inferior ovary; Oleaceae lacks stipules and has a superior ovary.

comparisons.title: Ash vs boxelder
comparisons.rule: Fraxinus makes single samaras; Acer negundo makes paired samaras.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not teach Oleaceae as 'opposite leaves + four white petals'; the local focal genera often have reduced or absent corollas.
